payload.output: Whether water is wet depends on definition. If wet means having water on a surface, water itself is not wet — it makes other things wet. If wet means being a liquid or being in contact with liquid, then water is wet. There is no single scientifically agreed-upon answer.
payload.context: Wetness is typically defined as the condition of being covered or saturated with a liquid, most commonly water. In physics and chemistry, wetness relates to the ability of a liquid to maintain contact with a solid surface through adhesion and surface tension. Whether water itself is considered wet is a topic of informal debate with no definitive scientific consensus.
